name: Dig to the Core
subtitle: Incremental digging game
promotional_text: Shovel, drill, laser. Dig straight down through clay, fossils, a dinosaur graveyard and lava lakes, all 240 metres to the middle of the Earth.
description:
You start in a sunny field beside a supply shack. Straight down is the whole planet. Start digging.

Every bit of rock you dig out pays. Deeper rock is harder and pays more, ore veins glint in your headlamp, and buried finds pop out for a lump sum. Spend it at the shack on better tools and a crew, then go deeper: ten layers, 240 metres, all the way to the core.

- Dig anywhere: the ground really comes away where you aim
- Seven tools: shovel, pickaxe, jackhammer, drill, dynamite, laser drill and the Earth-Borer
- Ten layers, each with its own rock: topsoil, clay, bedrock, a fossil bed, a dinosaur graveyard, crystal caves, lava lakes, the mantle and the core
- Sixteen buried finds to dig up
- A crew of moles and robo-moles that keep digging while you shop
- A mine lift that rides down to your deepest point
- A real ending when you dig out the core, in about 30 to 60 minutes; your progress saves as you go

Free to play with ads. Watching an ad for a boost (2x digging, a crew rush, extra cash) is always your choice, and a short ad can appear at natural breaks. You never need to watch one or buy anything to finish. A one-time purchase removes the ads and doubles your digging for good.
